findings.description: list(set(found)) throws away the order in which products were found, which contradicts the docstring's promise that the first query's best match comes first; the order is arbitrary, so the [:limit] cut keeps arbitrary items.
applies_to uses > where the comment says the discount applies to baskets of at least min_basket_cents, so a basket exactly at the threshold gets no discount.
The VAT rate is divided by 100 before it is passed to apply_vat, which expects a percentage (0-100), so NL VAT comes out as 0.21% instead of 21% and gross is almost equal to net.
geocode.locate returns None for an unknown city, so unpacking it raises TypeError instead of InvalidOrder; a point outside every zone likewise lets ValueError escape from zone_for.
Fields are joined with commas and never quoted or escaped, which contradicts the docstring's RFC 4180 claim; a city or field containing a comma or a quote corrupts the CSV.
revenue // len(todays) raises ZeroDivisionError on a day with no orders, where the field comment says the average should be 0.
first_page asks for page=0, but pages are numbered from 1, so start becomes -size and the slice _ORDERS[-size:0] is always empty.
biggest_orders sorts the list from repo.all_orders() in place, although callers must not modify it, so the repository's oldest-first order is permanently changed.
locate returns (latitude, longitude), but the tuple is unpacked as lon, lat, so zone_for gets swapped coordinates and returns the wrong zone or raises ValueError.
total_weight returns grams, but rate_for expects kilograms, so postage is about 1000 times too high and any parcel over 30 g raises FreightRequired.
range(1, attempts) makes only attempts-1 calls; with attempts=1 the function is never called and `raise last` raises TypeError, because last is None.

business_days_between counts days from start up to but not including end, while the docstring says after start up to and including end; for example, Saturday to Monday returns 0 instead of 1, and Friday to Monday returns 1 for the wrong day.
